"multiplication_and_solver": "For certified generators, at homogenized degree d enumerate all semigroup exponents of degree-d products; retain lex-first product per exponent, exact subduction witnesses restore lower terms. Build full graded basis and multiplication table. Homogenize EVERY input equation to its exact least psi degree using symbolic subduction, retaining identity certificates. Construct full-column Khovanskii-Macaulay rows b*f_i at increasing degrees. Exact Gaussian elimination uses leftmost nonzero pivot, input row order (generator index, multiplier exponent); retain row-combination certificates. Construct quotient normal forms and multiplication matrices only with a verified border basis: closed monomial/order-ideal basis, invertible basis block, all border reductions certified in the source ideal, commuting multiplication matrices, and each original ideal generator evaluates to the zero operator. If criterion fails increase d, retain all prior cost; no rank-stabilization-only shortcut. Recover finite F_p points by lexicographic exact factorization/joint eigenspace splitting of multiplication matrices; retain nonreduced multiplicities. Use t0 only as a homogenized degree tag and solve the entire affine t0=1 chart. Never invert a nonconstant phi or discard its zero locus; affine boundary points such as u=0 remain in this chart. Projective t0=0 points are explicitly outside the original affine problem, not lost affine solutions. Any optional localization requires explicit complement-chart solving with full charges. Rational x tuples recover as all ordered roots, with multiplicity, of T^m-e1*T^(m-1)+...+(-1)^m*em; lift all y and independently test signed group sums. Every rejected algebraic tuple and its reason is retained. For deterministic finite root extraction, scan every lambda in F_p for kernels of each multiplication operator minus lambda*I, refining joint eigenspaces in coordinate order; count all scans and nilpotent handling. Lexicographic polynomial factorization may be used only if the exact algorithm and version are frozen in the execution lock and charged; no hidden random solver choice. If the certified ideal contains1, archive its explicit source-generator combination and return an empty quotient and empty solution list; do not attempt multiplication matrices of dimension0. A quotient dimension or matrix rank alone never certifies UNSAT.",

"same_symmetry_control": "Run conventional full-column Macaulay/border-basis solver directly in e1,...,em on exactly the same symmetric equations, with the same exact certificate/recovery policy. Also run the same phi coordinate presentation with its defining ideal from exact elimination and ordinary monomial columns. A saving only against x coordinates is attributed to known symmetry or presentation, not a new semigroup advantage. On coefficient-randomized nulls compare the exact algebraic solution sets of the randomized equations; do not apply an ECC group-sum filter or label those null roots as group relations. Rational base membership and all multiplicity/permutation recovery remain identical.",

"direct_solver": "Ordinary full-column Macaulay/border-basis solve on (f,g(x1),...,g(xm)) in x coordinates, same pivot/row/degree rules, finite-root recovery and independent group check. Identity valuation slice must reproduce matrices/rows/solutions exactly. Deterministic exhaustive group tuple enumeration is a separately timed acquisition/checking comparator, not supplied to any solver."

"triangularization": "For every zero-dimensional clique ideal compute reduced lex Groebner basis. If1 occurs, retain its ideal-membership witness and return empty component. Otherwise recursively choose the least remaining variable and its monic elimination polynomial. Use gcd/subresultant regularization to split earlier triangular factors exactly when a leading coefficient or discriminant is zero on one component; retain both zero/nonzero branches with Bezout regularity witnesses. Squarefree each univariate fibre using derivative/gcd, record characteristic2 Frobenius-root steps when needed, and keep products of factors whenever the next polynomial coefficients remain regular. Continue until each component is a monic squarefree triangular chain. Branches are lex sorted; verify union equality to the input ideal by computing the intersection of component ideals with an elimination selector and checking mutual Groebner reductions. This is polynomial triangularization, not interpolation from a solution lookup table. Point decomposition is permitted only when algebraic splitting actually forces it, and its full size/cost is charged.",
